name: Quebrada de las Señoritas
why: From a 17th-century village church up a dry riverbed into a canyon of red clay towers.
book: Free, no permit. Buses from Humahuaca to Uquía take 10-15 minutes.
water: None after the village: carry 1.5 litres, the sun is strong at 2,800 m.
dangers: After summer storms the riverbed can flood: do not enter if rain is coming.
Sun and dry air: hat and sun cream.
Soft clay walls: do not climb them.
turnaround: Back out of the canyon before afternoon storms in the rainy months; otherwise none.

points.name: Uquía church
points.note: San Francisco de Paula, with its paintings of angels carrying arquebuses. Walk south of the church on Padre Lozano past the cemetery.

points.name: Mouth of the Quebrada de las Señoritas
points.note: Where the dirt road ends, about 1 km from the church; from here you walk up the dry riverbed.

points.name: Red canyon of the Quebrada de las Señoritas
points.note: Near the end of the canyon: the tallest red towers. Best in morning light.
